title: I used AI to build a surprisingly feature-filled GTA-style game in ~30 days. Meet Temu GTA.
author: ledniv
selftext:
# I used AI to build a GTA-style game in ~30 days. Meet Temu GTA 😂

**Play it here:** [**https://gta.nitzan.games**](https://gta.nitzan.games/)

For the past month, I've been using Astra to build **Grand Total Anarchy**, a GTA-style game that runs entirely in the browser.

I provided the direction, requested features, played the game, and gave feedback. Astra wrote all the code, created the artwork, implemented the gameplay, tested it, and even made the trailer.

Here's what we ended up with:

* 🌎 A large connected island with cities, countryside, airports, and a military base.
* 🚗 37 vehicle models, including cars, motorcycles, buses, helicopters, and airplanes.
* 🔫 Weapons, combat, and five levels of police pursuit.
* 📖 A 31-chapter story campaign about saving your aunt Rosa's garage.
* 🚕 Taxi jobs, pizza deliveries, bus routes, and other activities.
* 🚶 Pedestrians with daily activities and behaviors.
* 🎮 Multiplayer deathmatch with vehicles and weapons.

**Here is how I built it.**

The project started as a much smaller driving sandbox. Rather than asking Astra to build a complete GTA game in one shot, we kept expanding it over roughly a month.

I used my [Data-Oriented Design skill](https://github.com/Data-Oriented-Design-for-Games/data-oriented-design), which is based on the architecture from my upcoming Manning book. It guides the AI to separate data, logic, and presentation, use arrays and indices instead of complex object hierarchies, and avoid allocations in the game loop.

Having a consistent architecture was important as the project grew. Otherwise, adding new features could easily turn the codebase into a mess.

**The workflow was basically:**

1. Describe a feature or area I wanted.
2. Have Astra plan and implement it.
3. Have Astra run automated tests and review the result in the actual browser.
4. Play it myself and provide feedback.
5. Repeat.

A big part of this was making Astra responsible for testing its own work, not just writing code.

For example, here are some prompts you can use to set up a similar workflow (these are example prompts, not verbatim copies of mine):

**For the initial game:**

>Build a GTA-style driving sandbox using Three.js. Start with a small playable city, a character who can walk around, and cars that can be stolen and driven. Use the Data-Oriented Design skill for the architecture. Keep it playable throughout development.

**For adding features:**

>Implement the feature, then run the game and test it in the browser. Capture screenshots, inspect the results, identify problems, fix them, and repeat. Don't consider the feature complete just because the code runs.

**For expanding the world:**

>Expand the map with distinct neighborhoods, roads, landmarks, and activities. Make sure everything connects into one continuous world. Test vehicle navigation, pedestrian paths, collisions, and camera behavior.

**For testing existing systems:**

>Build automated tests for the gameplay systems, including missions, vehicles, damage, saving/loading, and multiplayer. Test success and failure paths. Fix issues found during testing, and verify that existing features still work.

The important part was the continuous iteration. Astra built automated simulation tests, used Playwright to interact with the game, captured screenshots, and reviewed its own results. I could then focus more on playing the game and deciding what needed improvement.

**Even the trailer was made entirely by Astra!**

It created a system to stage and capture gameplay footage, control cameras, generate a soundtrack using Python, and assemble everything with FFmpeg. The footage is actual in-game rendering, not AI-generated video.

**Now for the reality check.**

I call it **Temu GTA** for a reason. 😂

The game has a surprising amount of functionality, but it's still missing a LOT of polish. The driving, combat, animations, AI, and missions all need more work. Having a feature implemented is very different from having a feature that feels great.

Still, it's pretty amazing how much AI can build when you give it a clear direction, a consistent architecture, and a way to test its own work.

And I think that's what makes this exciting. You don't need to start by asking AI to build an entire game. Start with something small and playable, give it the tools and architecture to keep the code manageable, and expand from there.

**Give Temu GTA a try:** [**https://gta.nitzan.games**](https://gta.nitzan.games/)

I'd love to hear what you think, especially what works surprisingly well and what still feels like it came straight from Temu. 😂

comments.author: ContemptOfTheZ
comments.body:
Hey there, man. I'm actually a big fan of open world games, especially GTA clones, so played the game and this my feedback. First of all, kudos to you because I'm sure games like this are a massive undertaking. But you're right, the game needs polish but it can get pretty solid. Hope this works.

 

1. Visually is nice. Reminds me of [Krunker.io](http://Krunker.io) for some reason. Though it's a bit too yellow-colored. Maybe make it a bit colourful if you're going for this approach.

 

2. Add a map option. Can't be a GTA clone without one. If you can copy the GPS thingy from new games would be good.

 

3. Performance needs polish. Even when everything was lowered, it was quite the struggle for a browser game. My computer aint' that old. 

 

4. Not being able to bump into pedestrians isn't good.

 

5. Pedestrians need to be a bit smarter. Just at the start, three were stuck walking forward to the wall behind the Palm Pizza shop and wouldn't move.

 

6. Water visuals need a rework ASAP because it's just a blueish void.

 

7.  Police system needs [rework.You](http://rework.You) get reported way too easily. There's an alley behind Rosa's garage and I hit a dude carrying a box and immediately got reported. Turned around the corner and there were two cops already shooting at me. While I understand the police system provides excitement, it needs to be done right. For example, in Vice City, one star will have a cop chase you with a baton.

 

8. Motor bike steering also needs a rework. You fall too easily so it doesn't feel good when driving at high speeds.

 

9. Steering sounds also need rework. One sounds like a cat clawing at a cardboard and some others like a whisper or moan. This was noticeable in the Palm Bay Lookout area.

 

10. Some cars will be parked in the middle of the street or sidewalk. Saw  one in the Suburbs, in front of Cedar Park.

 

11. Car damage visuals need improvement.

 

12. No money bar?

 

13. The aesthetic of the city is very good. I'll improve upon that and utilise hills more.

 

14. No ambient noises, only engine sounds. Maybe seagulls, chatter or random music playing in certain areas will be good.

 

15. In the police station in front of Mercado de Marina, there's a floating sign. It saying "2 star trespass" breaks immersion and I think it was a bug.

 

16. Helicopter controls are weird.

 

17. Countryside area is way too empty.

 

18. The North Ridge Airfield needs better lighting.

 

19. If you get out of the helicopter while in the air, the helicopter won't fall.

 

20. The sky has no stars or moon, or clouds.

 

21. Some times, when you crash into a solid object, like a rock, when driving a motorbike, you die right away instead of falling from the bike. That makes riding bikes very bad.

 

22. In the North Ridge area, near the Ridge Lookout, there's an oddly placed bench for the bus stop. 

 

23. In front of Palm Bay City Hall, there's a phallic-looking statue with a sign going through it.

 

24. Interiors are poorly lit, or simply don't have any lighting, like inside the museum.

 

25. Some pedestrians make weird sounds while others don't. This was also picked up in front of the museum area.

 

24. There are lots of unfinished areas.

 

25. Character can't jump.

 

26. Cops don't drop weapons

 

27. Pedestrians don't fight back,

 

28. When my character dies in the starting plaza after being gunned down, I re-spawned and saw my character there plus the cop cars that were chasing prior that. Dying should reset things.

replies.author: ledniv
replies.body:
Hey, thanks for the detailed response!

What do you mean by map options? There is a map and a minimap.

Also, what do you mean by bumping into pedestrians? You can run them over.

replies.author: ContemptOfTheZ
replies.body: Map as in an option to see the map itself. I couldn't find the option. Also, bumping into pedestrians when walking, not running them over. In GTA games, you usually bump into them and they say things or are staggered. You can add floating dialogue boxes when that happens so there's a reason to check them out and give the city a more "looking alive" vibe.

comments.author: Any_Ad_3141
comments.body: I think there are a lot of people who look down on ai coding and they have absolutely no clue what they are talking about. They say anything made with ai is "slop" and clearly it isn't. AI is a tool. If you know how to prompt it well, you can do amzaing things. You have been doing this for 30 days by yourself. GTA6 has taken 13 years with over 6,000 people working on it. All of these people dogging AI need to close thier mouths because they are proving how little they know. I have spent the last 10 months with AI building an app to run my printing company. It has a ton of things I could not find from a "software company" and I'm adding additonal features every day. Clients have a client portal and can do far more now than they can on almost any other printing companie's website. I have no coding experience, but I know how to explain things and can think through the complexities of what we are trying to achieve. Because of that, I have built something real that makes me money by making my company run better than ever. This is due 100% to AI and it's "slop" coding. Keep jamming on this thing. It's fun. It may not be GTA6, but the fact is that it doesn't have to be. Thanks for sharing this project.

replies.author: M_O_Z_G
replies.body: Regardless of holy war, comparing solving a utilitarian in-house business problem with developing technically complex creative products for a wide audience — these are slightly different cases. It's like saying that a shovel is universally good for eating because I dug a pound of gold out of the ground with it.

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body:
This is 1) technologically impressive for 30 days, 2) objectively a terrible game, 3) it's terrible in an entertaining fashion but outside of a short burst of LOL you're right it's got along way to go before it's there. 

Did play it, was good for a giggle, the impressive part to me is the tech involved, it let's someone with the knowledge to leverage the tools properly accomplish amazing things in short periods of time. 

Look forward to seeing the finished game. Be well and keep creating.
